newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU welcomes proposed shake-up of United Nations.
newsitem.headline: EU welcomes proposed shake-up of United Nations.

text.p: The European Union has welcomed a proposed radical shake up of the United Nations, which it said aimed to put the U.N. in a position to play "a fully effective, transparent, responsible and dependable role".

"The EU notes with satisfaction that the Secretary-General's propositions treat in depth questions relating to development, humanitarian activities and human rights," the Luxembourg EU Presidency said in a statement issued late on Wednesday.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan promised on Wednesday the biggest reform in the world body's history, pledging to overhaul bureaucracy, shrink budgets, merge programmes and put savings to work in poor nations.
In a 90-page document Annan said the U.N. was becoming increasingly "fragmented, duplicative and rigid," often unable to meet expectations with accomplishments.

"This (reform) effort engages the credibility of the U.N. and its member states. They must commit themselves to bringing adequate replies to the questions with which we are confronted ...by the Secretary-General," the EU statement said.

It added that the success of reform required not only a rationalistation and a simplification of U.N. operations but also a reinforcement of the organisation based on "certain and foreseeable financial resources".
"The EU will study carefully the different propositions in the document which has been presented and offer its comments...during the general debate of the 52nd General Assembly," it added.
